sections.h2: Who does what on a Columbia County bill
sections.html:
The appraiser supplies values and exemptions. Local taxing bodies adopt budgets and millage, and the tax collector, based in Lake City, mails bills and takes payment.

The tax collector's main line is 386-758-1077, and the Tax Department answers at 386-758-1080. For value or exemption questions, dial the appraiser at (386) 758-1083. The Clerk of Court, at 386-719-7580 for tax deed questions, runs the deed sales that follow long delinquency.

The regular annual bill is due by March 31, and unpaid taxes generally turn delinquent April 1. The bill arrives in November, and the early-payment discount opens at 4% that month and falls a point each month through February.

The notice that arrives in August is a TRIM notice. It is a proposal, not the payment bill, so use it to check values, exemptions and hearing dates. When a due date lands on a weekend or holiday, Florida law gives qualifying payments next-working-day treatment, though a close call deserves a phone call.

The collector's year-at-a-glance calendar is a planning guide, and late-mailed bills, weekends and holidays can move a deadline, so follow the dates on your own notice.

  • April 1: unpaid taxes generally become delinquent, and tangible personal property returns are due to the appraiser.
  • April 30: installment applications are due.
  • May: delinquent-tax advertising and certificate sale preparation begin.
  • June 30 and September 30: the first two installments fall due.
  • November: annual collection starts at the 4% discount.

You can pay online, by phone, at the counter, through the mail, or at the Lake City drive-through and drop box. The office lists a 2.5% card fee with a $2 minimum and a $1.50 e-check fee for online or phone payments, and receives no part of the card fee.

  • Search by owner name, address or account number in the property tax portal.
  • If a mortgage escrow pays your tax, confirm the lender paid the right year, to avoid a duplicate payment.
  • E-billing is available, registered one property account at a time.
  • A duplicate notice can go to a second recipient, but the owner remains responsible.

The plan lets an owner prepay the current year in four payments if estimated tax is over $100 per notice. Submit Form DR-534 to the tax collector by April 30. The first payment confirms participation.

The first two installments use prior-year tax as the estimate, and later ones adjust to actual tax. A late first installment is accepted through July 31 without the June discount. The plan doesn't cover delinquent taxes.

On current taxes, an owner can sign a partial-payment agreement with the office and pay in pieces from November 1 through March 31. No early-payment discounts apply, and the full balance must be paid by March 31.

Tracking is your job, because the local plan mails no balance reminder before April 1. Any unpaid balance becomes delinquent with interest and costs, and partial payments do not stop a certificate sale if real estate tax remains unpaid. State law leaves partial payments to the tax collector's discretion before delinquency.

The Property Appraiser decides homestead, disability, widow or widower, military service, senior and agricultural benefits. March 1 is the usual filing deadline. The homestead exemption reaches $50,000, and its first $25,000 also lowers school tax.

Save Our Homes ties a homestead's yearly assessment growth to 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is lower, and the next January 1 after a sale brings the parcel back to just value. A disabled ex-servicemember may take a $5,000 cut in assessed value. A former servicemember aged 65 or over with a lasting service-connected disability may receive a discount matching the VA disability rating. A deferral request for homestead tax is filed with the collector by March 31 after the assessment year.

The tax collector's page also mentions income-based help and certain vacancy reductions for service assessments. Call to confirm which one fits.

sections.h2: Unpaid tax at a house closing
sections.html:
Closing agents usually pay the current year out of the seller's proceeds, and the collector can confirm what posted. Ask for an exact payoff for your closing date, since interest and costs change the amount.

A tax certificate is a lien and doesn't transfer ownership. Under section 197.502 a certificate holder can seek a tax deed two years after April 1 of the issue year, and the clerk's office holds the sale. Redemption is available until a tax deed is issued, unless the buyer has paid the clerk in full, so call the Tax Department at 386-758-1080 with your parcel number before any sale date. The office accepts cash, money order, cashier's check or card for certificate redemption and cautions against assuming a personal check works.

Besides value-based tax, the bill can carry non-ad valorem assessments for services such as fire, solid waste, paving or lighting, depending on the parcel's location. The county, city or district that creates an assessment sets it, and the tax collector only bills what the tax roll certifies.

Business equipment is a different account. Returns generally reach the appraiser by April 1, and unpaid accounts can lead to tax warrants rather than a certificate sale. Anyone selling a house that hosted a business should ask both offices whether an equipment account is open under the same name.

Mailing addresses are another trap. The tax roll address comes from the Property Appraiser, so a new owner who wants the November bill sent elsewhere should ask that office to update the record. The collector also takes a forwarding request.

Contact the Property Appraiser first, then use the Value Adjustment Board if needed. A value petition reaches the clerk within 25 days of the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes, and an exemption denial can be appealed in the 30 days after a denial letter goes out.

Payment questions and value disputes go to separate offices, and a petition does not replace paying the bill the tax collector sends in November.

Pull your latest bill and note whether you are on an installment plan. Ask the Tax Department for a payoff through your expected closing date, and give a copy to the title agent. Check that your mortgage lender, if it pays from escrow, has paid the right year. After closing, send the collector a forwarding address and keep the paid receipt with your settlement papers. A cash sale skips lender underwriting, but the tax payoff and the lien release work the same way.

faqs.q: What date makes Columbia County tax delinquent?
faqs.a: The ordinary annual bill must be paid by March 31, and April 1 usually starts delinquency. Discounts run from 4% in November to 1% in February.

faqs.q: How do I join the Columbia County installment plan?
faqs.a: File Form DR-534 with the collector by April 30. Estimated tax must top $100 per notice, and your first payment confirms participation.

faqs.q: What card fee does the Columbia County tax collector charge?
faqs.a: The office lists a 2.5% card fee with a $2 minimum, plus a $1.50 e-check fee, for online or phone payments.

faqs.q: Which number covers a Columbia County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Call the Property Appraiser at (386) 758-1083. March 1 is the usual filing deadline.

faqs.q: Who runs tax deed sales in Columbia County?
faqs.a: The Clerk of Court conducts them and issues deeds to winning bidders. Tax deed questions go to 386-719-7580.
